steps.title: Centre every servo
steps.html:
1. Plug each servo into the PCA9685 and run the servo centring sketch. Every servo goes to 90°.
  2. Leave them centred. Don't turn the shafts by hand after this.
  3. Fit the horns later so that at 90° the femur is level and the tibia points straight down, like the finished model.

Label each servo with a bit of tape: L1-coxa, L1-femur, L1-tibia, and so on.

steps.title: Bearings into the body
steps.html:
1. Flip the body upside down.
  2. Press an MR85ZZ bearing into the round seat under each of the 6 hip pockets until it sits flush.

Too loose? A tiny drop of superglue on the outside edge. Too tight? Warm the seat with a hair dryer.

steps.title: Brass inserts
steps.html:
1. 4 inserts into the tops of the tall lid posts.
  2. 8 inserts into the short PCA9685 posts on the floor.
  3. Press straight down slowly until flush, then let them cool for 10 s.

Do the 6 feet now too: 2 inserts each in the top face.

steps.title: Hip servos
steps.html:
1. Stand each servo's plug on its edge and push it out through the inner slot (the one facing the middle of the body).
  2. Lower the servo in with the shaft on the outside end. Tabs sit flush in the recess.
  3. 2 × M2.5×6 screws through the tabs. Snug, not tight.

steps.title: Electronics bay
steps.html:
1. On PCA9685 #2, solder the A0 jumper closed so its address is 0x41. #1 stays 0x40.
  2. Screw #1 on the left posts (legs 1–3) and #2 on the right (legs 4–6), servo headers facing outwards.
  3. Solder a 1000 µF cap across each board's V+ / GND terminal (stripe = GND).
  4. Slide the C3 into its fence with USB-C through the front wall. Zip-tie the two Mini560s at front-left.

steps.title: Coxa brackets (Leg_A)
steps.html:
1. Femur servo into each Leg_A first: plug out through the slot, tabs flush, 2 × M2.5×6.
  2. Screw a double-arm horn to the underside of the top plate through the slots (2 × M2×6), lined up with the leg.
  3. Hook the bracket over the hip servo: horn onto the spline, centre screw through the top hole.
  4. From below: washer, then the shaft pin up through the bottom plate into the body bearing. 2 × M2×5 hold the pin disc.

Leg numbers go anticlockwise from front-left, seen from above.

steps.title: Femurs (Leg_B)
steps.html:
1. Press a bearing into the floor of each femur servo pocket on Leg_A and each knee pocket on Leg_B.
  2. Knee servo into Leg_B (plug out the slot toward the femur, tabs flush, 2 × M2.5×6).
  3. Horn onto the Leg_B horn arm, slide the fork over the femur servo, horn onto the spline, centre screw.
  4. Washer + shaft pin through the other arm into the bearing. Femur should be level.

steps.title: Tibia brackets + claws
steps.html:
1. Claw into the socket under each Leg_C_1, 2 × M2×8 from inside into the foot inserts.
  2. Horn on the bracket's horn arm, slide it over the knee servo, horn onto the spline, centre screw.
  3. Washer + shaft pin into the knee bearing. The claw should point straight down.

steps.title: Servo wiring
steps.html:
1. Each leg plugs into 3 channels in a row: coxa, femur, tibia.
  2. PCA #1: leg 1 → ch 0-2, leg 2 → ch 3-5, leg 3 → ch 6-8.
    PCA #2: leg 4 → ch 0-2, leg 5 → ch 3-5, leg 6 → ch 6-8.
  3. Brown wire = GND, toward the board edge.
  4. Femur + tibia leads run up over the hip bracket and in through the lid notch. Leave a loop of slack so the hip can swing ±35°.

steps.title: Power + brain wiring
steps.html:
1. Battery + → switch → both Mini560 IN+. Battery − → both IN−.
  2. Mini560 #1 OUT → PCA #1 V+ terminal. Mini560 #2 OUT → PCA #2. Never join the two outputs.
  3. Mini560 #1 OUT+ also → C3 5V pin (GND → GND).
  4. I²C chain: C3 GND, 3V3, SDA GPIO8, SCL GPIO9 → PCA #2 → PCA #1 (same pins on both ends of each board).
  5. Battery sense: switched + → 100k → GPIO3 → 47k → GND.

Check every red wire with a multimeter before the first power-up. Reversed polarity kills the Mini560.

steps.title: Lid + battery
steps.html:
1. Push the switch into the back of the lid.
  2. Feed the battery lead up through the hole in the lid top.
  3. Drop the lid on (cables through the 6 notches) and screw the 4 M2×6 into the post inserts.
  4. Strap the battery on top and plug the Deans in last.

steps.title: Remote: inside
steps.html:
1. Set the MT3608 to 5.0 V first with a multimeter (brass screw).
  2. Battery into its bay, TP4056 into the pocket with USB-C out the back.
  3. ESP32 rests on the end ledges with its USB-C out the back. MT3608 on foam tape in the right grip.

steps.title: Remote: wiring
steps.html:
1. Power: LiPo → TP4056 B+/B−. TP4056 OUT+ → switch → MT3608 IN+. MT3608 OUT → ESP32 5V + GND.
  2. All sticks, slider and knob: VCC → 3V3, GND → GND.
  3. Left stick X → 34, Y → 35, SW → 25. Right stick X → 32, Y → 33, SW → 26.
  4. Slider wiper → 36 (VP). Knob wiper → 39 (VN). Action button → 27 and GND.

Only GPIO 32-39 for anything analog: the others stop working while ESP-NOW is on.

steps.title: Remote: close it up
steps.html:
1. Joysticks onto their posts (4 × M2×6 each, into inserts). Slider, knob, button and switch into their holes.
  2. Lower the top onto the bottom; the lip locates it. 6 × M2×8 from underneath.

steps.title: First power-up
steps.html:
1. Robot on its back or on a box so the legs hang free.
  2. Remote on first, then the robot.
  3. It stands up slowly. Try the sticks gently, then put it on the floor.

Unplug the robot battery when you're done. Charge it on the IMAX B3, never on the TP4056.
